summary: Analyze max-torque-at-small-error capability: current state, candidate integral mechanisms, math verification

current.summary: Ran 258+ firmware-exact sim runs (pid_algorithm_sim.c, V=200, kp=2000 kd=350000, 10 s, seeds 1-3, overflow_violations=0 in every run). CURRENT (step2, 25% I-clamp): never hunts under any load 0.14-0.42, but the rotor sticks within 2-8 ms of load application at a standing error set by the clamp ceiling, not by ki: 6.3k counts (0.19% rev) at 0.14 N*m, 9.3k (0.29%) at 0.20, 23.5k (0.72%) at 0.30, 42.7k (1.30%) at 0.38; full torque (0.40 N*m) is only reached at error >= 39,322 counts = 1.20% rev. At Tom's target error of 3,277 counts (0.1% rev) step2's sustained torque ceiling is 0.124 N*m = 31% of stall (analytic, validated by the sim curve to within 1%). OLD (100% clamp): sustains 100% torque at any error given ~40 ms windup (ki=25), but limit-cycles violently (std ~1,700-3,300 counts, 7-22 Hz, all seeds) for every load in 0.14-0.26 N*m — exactly the band where full torque minus load exceeds static friction (0.40-0.13=0.27) — and it holds quiet loads 0.28-0.38 at PERMANENT full-rail drive (V=200, 90-deg lead) with seed-dependent standing error 0.9k-18k counts. ki (5/25/100) changes step2's standing error <2x and never removes it (error static to 4 digits between last-1s and last-0.5s windows); windup delay is milliseconds (I rails in 1.8-13 ms measured; analytic t=max_I/(ki*e) ticks) and is NOT the bottleneck — the clamp ceiling is. Intermediate clamps: 50% gives 0.224 N*m (56%) at 3,277 counts and does not hunt UNDER load, but the no-load post-move limit cycle returns already at a 31.25% clamp (post-move rms ~3,000 at 20 Hz vs 39-117 at 25%), so no fixed-clamp setting materially beats the current one without reintroducing the original complaint. Low-stiction plant (0.03): old stops hunting violently (std 103-280) and holds ~0 error; step2 standing error persists (3.2k at 0.10, 10.5k at 0.20, 23.5k at 0.30), confirming the equilibrium law |tau(P(e)+I_rail) - load| <= static_friction. Loads >= 0.40 N*m: both algs lose position in the first transient (true error 63k at 0.40, ~128k at 0.42 — CSV error column is clamped at 52,428, recovered from desired-actual) then hold indefinitely with ~zero drift.
current.verdict: No — with the current firmware (step2, 25% integral clamp) the motor cannot apply anywhere near maximum torque at a 0.1%-of-rev error: at 3,277 counts the sustained ceiling is ~0.124 N*m = 31% of stall at V=200 (and ~29% of the V=80 ceiling at the firmware-default voltage), and full torque only becomes available once the error has grown to ~1.2% of a revolution; the windup DELAY Tom asks about is a non-issue (the integral rails in 2-13 ms at ki=5..100), the problem is the windup CEILING. The old firmware did deliver 100% torque at small error after ~40 ms, but only by allowing I to reach full authority, which is exactly what produced the violent 17-21 Hz stick-slip hunt for every load between ~0.14 and ~0.27 N*m (and no-load after moves) plus permanent full-power heating while holding; and simply raising the clamp cannot fix this — the no-load limit cycle already returns at a 31.25% clamp on this plant, because any sustained I-torque above breakaway friction (~0.13 N*m) re-arms the stick-slip cycle. So the current design sits at the practical optimum of the fixed-clamp approach, and meeting Tom's requirement (near-full torque at 0.1% error) requires a different mechanism than a bigger fixed clamp (e.g. error/velocity-gated integration), noting any such mechanism that lets I approach full authority must also lower PID_MAX_AUTHORITY_PRE_SHIFT (e.g. to ~500e6; real authority never exceeds 390<<19=204.5e6) to preserve the int32 no-overflow proof — a 50% clamp still fits the current proof (sum 2.0e9 < 2^31) but 100% (2.4e9) does not.

TASK 1 mechanism (validated by all data): stick-slip equilibrium law. The rotor sticks wherever |tau_motor(e) - load| <= static_friction (0.13 N*m default). step2: I rails at 25% (26,214,400 pre-shift = 12,800 output counts) within ms, so sustained output = (2000*e + 26,214,400)>>11 and the error CANNOT shrink below the value where that torque comes within 0.13 of the load — hence the large, permanent standing errors. old: I keeps winding to 100%, torque grows to full 0.40; if 0.40 - load > 0.13 the rotor breaks away, overshoots, re-sticks, re-winds => 17-22 Hz limit cycle (loads 0.14-0.26); if 0.40 - load <= 0.13 (loads 0.28-0.38) it sticks at a path-dependent error (per-seed old values, e.g. 0.28: +14,261/+868/+4,165; 0.32: +4,435/+18,277/+18,198) while driving PERMANENT full rail (mean voltage 200, mean output 52k-69k, lead clamped 90 deg = max heating forever to hold a static load).

Analytic curve out(e)=(2000e+26,214,400)>>11 reproduces every sim point to ~1%; full torque requires e >= 39,322 counts = 1.20% rev.
old (when not hunting, loads 0.28-0.38): sustained tau = 0.400 (100%) at EVERY settled error from 868 to 42,636 counts — full torque at any error, because I alone rails the output.
AT e = 3,277 counts (0.1% rev): step2 = (2000*3277+26,214,400)>>11 = 16,000 out -> V=62, lead 16,000 (87.9 deg, sin 0.999) -> 0.124 N*m = 31% of stall. 50% clamp = 28,800 out -> V=112, lead clamped -> 0.224 N*m = 56% (sim interpolation between bracketing settled points gave exactly 0.224 — analytic curve independently validated). old / 100% clamp = 54,400 -> railed 51,200 -> 0.400 N*m = 100% (but see hunt zone and full-rail heating). Note: no load in the whole sweep produced a step2 settled error below 6,331 counts — any load that moves the rotor at all leaves step2 with >= ~2x Tom's target error.

NO-LOAD STABILITY BOUNDARY vs clamp (resolves 'can we just raise the clamp'): pure standstill with no stimulus never winds I (peak_i < 1% authority) and is quiet for ALL clamps incl. old — the historical no-load cycle needs residual post-move error to wind I. With a 1-rot move (--move 1 --move-time 1), seeds 1-3: clamp 25% (current): post_move_rms 39-117 counts, no oscillation. Clamp 31.25% (frac 5/16): post_move_rms 2,804-3,024 at 19.9-20.4 Hz — limit cycle already back (peak_i pinned at exactly the 32,768,000 clamp). 37.5%/50%/100%/old: same ~3,000 rms 20 Hz cycle. So the stability boundary on this plant is between 25% and 31.25% — TIGHTER than the prior '>=37.5%' note. Physical reason: I-only torque at the clamp must stay below breakaway friction (25% -> 0.094 N*m < 0.13 with margin; 31.25% -> 0.124, margin ~4%, noise+P pushes it over). Consequence: for ANY fixed clamp, sustained I-torque is capped near the static-friction torque (~0.13 N*m = 33% of stall), so torque-at-small-error cannot be materially improved by clamp tuning alone.

TASK 6 — V=80 analytic picture (sim CANNOT run this: MAX_PWM_V is a compile-time #define 200 at pid_algorithm_sim.c line 60, no CLI flag). authority = 80<<19 = 41,943,040 (< 800e6 cap). zerocross.summary: Implemented a zero-crossing-gated integral windup mechanism in a copy of pid_algorithm_sim.c (repo untouched; gate-off output verified bit-identical to pristine sim). Four gate modes tested (clamp/freeze/bleed + a new 'avg' mode invented after CSV analysis). Plain clamp/freeze/bleed all fail load-holding: freeze produces a 4.5 Hz relaxation oscillation (std ~9,300) because static friction forces I to wind to breakaway torque (0.33 N·m) which then overshoots the hold torque (0.20); clamp/bleed relax back to step2's ~9.5k-count error. The CSV showed successive zero-crossing I values (79M / 30M) bracket the true hold-need (52.4M) symmetrically, motivating the winner: 'avg' mode — on each zero crossing set I to the midpoint of its values at this and the previous crossing, freeze integration 0.1 s, and only allow I past the 25% rail toward full authority after the error has kept one sign (beyond a ±1000-count deadband) for 0.1 s. Winner config (avg, holdoff=3125 ticks, deadband=1000 counts) scorecard at kp=2000/kd=350000/V=200, >=3 seeds each: S1 no-load ki{10,25,100} PASS (err std 32.9-33.0 = noise floor, osc 0, gate dormant — identical to step2); S2 load 0.20 settled mean 577-662 counts (db=500 variant: 98-197) vs step2's 9,043-9,509, std 33, settle 0.11-0.57 s; S2 load 0.30 @ sf 0.13 physically impossible for ANY controller (breakaway 0.43 > tau_max 0.40) — identical error to step2 but gate wastes power (V=199.8 railed vs step2's 138.8); S3 no hunt (osc 0 vs old's 16.9-18.8 Hz / std 2,836-2,934); S4 snap-back overshoot 2,165-2,263 vs step2 2,836-2,886 (22% BETTER) and fixes step2's hidden -2,700-count post-step park (gate: -235..-315); S5 post_move_rms {69.8,172.4,145.2,33.5,300.2} vs step2 {33.0,61.7,37.5,33.5,216.2} — comparable, worst seed slightly worse (static park inside deadband, no oscillation), move overshoot halved (1,193-1,261 vs 1,663-1,791); S6 sf=0.03: no-load all quiet 9/9, load 0.20 mean 470-494 (step2: 10,326-10,602), load 0.30 mean -8..+2.5 with std 158-321 micro-wander (step2 parks 23,490 away). Tom's exact scenario (0.1%-rev = 3,277-count step): old oscillates forever (std 3,080 @ 19-21 Hz), step2 parks 2,019-2,809 counts off FOREVER with I railed, gate parks at 749-915 (db=500: 330-420), quiet. overflow_violations=0 in all ~200 runs. Deadband robustness: db=500 hunts at ki<=10 (landing scatter > window); db=1000 validated across ki 5-100.
zerocross.verdict: A zero-crossing-gated integrator WORKS, but only the 'avg' variant: gate I past the 25% rail toward full authority after 0.1 s of one-signed error (beyond a ±1000-count deadband), and on each zero crossing set I to the midpoint of its values at the last two crossings (which self-tunes to the true hold torque of the symmetric stick-slip cycle) then freeze integration 0.1 s. This delivers both goals of the design brief: no-load behavior is bit-identical-quiet to step2 (the gate never opens on noise), and load-hold error drops from step2's ~9,500 counts (0.29% rev, held forever) to 100-900 counts (0.003-0.027% rev) in 0.11-0.57 s at load 0.20, while snap-back overshoot IMPROVES 22% and old-firmware hunting never returns. On Tom's exact 0.1%-rev question: the current step2 firmware cannot correct a 3,277-count error at all on the calibrated bench plant (P+25%-I rail = 0.125 N·m < 0.13 N·m breakaway — it parks ~2,000-2,800 counts off forever), whereas the gate corrects it to within the deadband (~750-900 counts; ~350-420 with the tighter db=500/ki>=25 tune). Hard limits to disclose: the mechanism's accuracy floor IS the deadband (errors under ~1,000 counts = 0.031% rev are deliberately left to P+25%I; well inside Tom's 0.1% spec but not zero); loads whose breakaway (load + static friction) exceeds max torque are unfixable by any controller and the gate then rails the output (V=200 vs step2's V=139) for no benefit; and the naive clamp/freeze/bleed modes from the original design intuition all fail — the midpoint-on-crossing rule is the load-bearing invention. Firmware port is ~10-15 extra instructions/tick + 4 int32 state words, but REQUIRES lowering PID_MAX_AUTHORITY_PRE_SHIFT from 800e6 to <=500e6 (free: real authority <=390<<19=204.5M) and computing the ki overflow cap against full authority, because I may now legitimately reach 100% of authority. Recommend bench validation next (especially sudden load removal, which the sim cannot express).

alternatives.summary: Evaluated 3 alternative load-holding mechanisms plus the pure clamp-raise trade-off against the current firmware (step2: 25% integral clamp + back-calculation), using the firmware-exact simulator (587 runs, 3-5 seeds each, ALL overflow_violations=0). Protocol note: a pure 8-s standstill is a trivially-passing test (I never winds, peak_i=0%), so every mechanism was probed with a post-move no-load test (2-rot profiled move, then 9 s observation) and a 0.61-rot snap-back step; the old-firmware anchor reproduced its known post-move limit cycle (RMS 2,458-3,034 vs briefing 2,500-4,400), validating the protocol. RESULTS: (A) Static clamp raise: the no-load limit cycle returns at 31.25% (frac 5/16) already — ki10 5/5 seeds, ki100 5/5, ki25 2/5 hunt — and identically at 37.5-100%; 25% is quiet 5/5 at all ki. The prior "37.5%+" finding is confirmed and tightened: the current 25% clamp sits with essentially ZERO headroom. Under load the trade-off is binary: at 0.20 Nm, fracs 4-10 all leave the SAME 9.0-9.5k-count standing error (rotor stuck inside the 0.13 Nm static-friction cone; breakaway needs 42,240 output counts), frac 12 drops it to 1.5-3.1k, frac 16 hunts at 20-21 Hz; at 0.30 Nm error falls 23.5k->17.7k->16.5k->9.6k->3.1k (frac 4->12). Every frac that helps under load hunts at no-load. (B) Two-tier windup (knee 25%, above-knee wind rate >>2/4/6, clamp 100%): fails everywhere — hunts post-move at no-load (shift 2: 5/9 seed-cases, shift 4: 3/9, shift 6: 1/9), hunts at 1.3-7.9 Hz under 0.20 load, gets STUCK at 18.3-21.8k error under 0.30 (slow torque rise lets the rotor stick where full rail 0.40-0.30=0.10 < 0.13 static — unrecoverable; back-calc also pins I at rail-P during saturation, nullifying the creep), and snap-back overshoot is 24.0-24.2k (shift 2/4, as bad as old fw) or 10.3-10.5k (shift 6) vs 2.85k current. (C) High-kP pure tuning (25% clamp kept): genuinely improves holding — standing error at 0.20: 6.9k/4.1k/2.7k/1.4k counts at kp 4000/8000/16000/32000 (kd 350000), at 0.30: 13.5k/9.4k/4.4k/2.9k; kp32000 keeps |err| <= 2,371 counts (0.072% rev) through the ENTIRE 0.20 load application with zero delay, and pure standstill stays at the 33-count noise floor with modest jitter growth (out_std 211->691, volt_std 0.7->1.7). BUT an abrupt 0.61-rot step latches a SUSTAINED full-rail relay oscillation: kp16000 430-451 Hz and kp32000 285-287 Hz on 5/5 seeds (output ±51,200, voltage swinging 0-200 with mean 175 — loud and hot), kp4000 hunts 18 Hz on 4/5 seeds, kp8000 on 2/5; raising kd (700k-2.1M) does not fix kp>=16000 and scaled kd (kp*175) itself screams at 289-452 Hz; kp32000/kd2.1M even screams after a profiled move. (D) Integral deadband 100-200 + 100% clamp: does NOT stay quiet — the limit cycle's error amplitude (~3k counts) dwarfs the deadband, which only gates noise-level errors; hunts post-move (db100: 8/9 seed-cases, db200: 3/9), hunts at 19-22 Hz while "holding" 0.20 (mean error ~-15 but std ~3.1k), bimodal 2.2k-17.7k at 0.30, snap-back overshoot 24.2k. None of the four alternatives cleanly beats the current 25% clamp.
alternatives.verdict: None of the alternative mechanisms beats the current 25%-clamp firmware for Tom's goal without breaking the thing the 25% clamp was chosen to fix: the static clamp has zero raise-headroom (the no-load cycle returns at 31.25%, one notch above the current setting, and only 75%+ actually reduces load error), two-tier windup is strictly dominated (hunts under load, sticks at ~20k counts at 0.30 Nm, old-firmware-grade 24k snap-back overshoot), and the integral deadband is ineffective because the limit cycle's amplitude (~3,000 counts) is 15-30x the deadband. The one mechanism with real substance is plain high kP: at kp=16000-32000 (kd kept at 350000, no firmware change) the motor holds 0.20/0.30 Nm to 1.4-2.9k counts (0.04-0.09% rev) instantly with no windup delay — kp=32000 never exceeds 0.072% of a rev during a 0.20 Nm load application — but it is disqualified as a drop-in default by a step-excited, sustained 285-450 Hz full-power relay oscillation (5/5 seeds at kp>=16000) that kd cannot damp. The bar for the parallel zero-crossing-gated integral is therefore: settled load error <= ~3.3k counts at 0.20/0.30 Nm (what frac-12 or kp16000 achieve), noise-floor quiet (err_std ~33) in post-move AND post-step no-load tests at ki 10/25/100 across >=5 seeds, and snap-back overshoot <= ~3k; if it clears that, it beats everything tested here. Two hard physics facts to carry into that design: (1) under 0.20 Nm, extra integral authority between 25% and 62.5% buys literally nothing (the rotor is stuck inside the static-friction cone until total output reaches ~42k counts), so a gated integral must be allowed to reach >=75% of authority to matter; (2) at 0.30 Nm this plant cannot break away once stuck far out (full rail gives 0.10 Nm net < 0.13 Nm static friction), so torque must develop FAST during the initial capture — mechanisms that wind slowly (two-tier) permanently lose. Any mechanism letting I reach ~69%+ of authority must also lower PID_MAX_AUTHORITY_PRE_SHIFT (frac<=10/16 fits the current 800e6 proof since (2+10/16)*800e6=2.1e9 < 2^31; frac 16 needs <=715e6; lowering to 500e6 is free because legal V<=390 gives real authority <=204.5e6).

critic.verdict: Tom's requirement — full motor torque available at 0.1% of a rotation (3,277 counts) of error — is NOT met by the current (step2) firmware and cannot be met by any static integral clamp: at V=200 the sustained ceiling at that error is 0.124 N·m = 31% of stall (and 28.6% of available at the V=80 default), because full torque needs P+I = 51,200 output counts while P contributes only 3,200 at 0.1% and the 25% I-rail adds 12,800; a static clamp large enough (>=93.75% of authority) is guaranteed to limit-cycle (the quiet ceiling is ~32% on the bench plant and LOWER on low-stiction units — 25% already hums at f_s<=0.10 in-sim) and would also overflow int32 unless PID_MAX_AUTHORITY_PRE_SHIFT is lowered (safe and free on M17 at <=600e6, but NOT free on M1/M2/M23 where the 800e6 cap binds — make it product-specific). The old firmware did meet the torque spec (100% after 41 ms at ki=25) but my sims confirm it bought little real holding: under constant loads below 0.27 N·m it hunts perpetually at 17-19 Hz (a ki-timescale relaxation cycle, not a resonance), and above 0.27 it freezes at a nonzero error just like step2 (identically ~51k counts at 0.39, where the physical output rail, not the I clamp, is binding). Practical framing for Tom: step2 today holds constant loads with settled error ≈ 1.024*((tau_L-0.022)/7.8125e-6 - 12,800) counts — 0.29%/0.72%/1.56% of a rev at 50%/75%/97.5% of stall torque — and keeps error <=0.1% only for loads up to ~0.15 N·m (~37% of stall); closing the gap requires either ~11-15x higher kP (stability unproven) or a state-dependent integral mechanism, and any such proposal must be re-checked against low-stiction units, sign-reversing (spring) loads, thermal limits of sustained stall torque, and the V=80 default — none of which the sim's single-bench-calibrated constant-load model can answer.

Bench: breakaway-torque measurement on N production units (slow current ramp at standstill until first motion, both directions), then rerun the fs sweep at fleet minimum. Bench: standstill captures at multiple rotor angles and temperatures via tools/pid_debug_capture.py. (3) Load type — everything here is constant-sign (gravity-like). A sign-reversing spring load makes the error cross zero, forcing the railed I to unwind through 2x26.2M at rate ki*|e| (a slow-reversal lag of 10s of ms to seconds at small error) and can re-enable hunting with the spring stiffness in the loop; completely unmodeled. Bench: weight-over-pulley (constant) vs spring/elastic rig (reversing), compare settled error and any oscillation. (4) Thermal — old's 100%-I 'wins' assume indefinite stall current; sustained 0.40 N*m at V=200 at zero speed dumps continuous I^2R into one phase pair (the M17 current limit exists partly for heating); the sim has no thermal model. Bench: sustained-hold soak at V=200 max output with winding/case temperature logging before recommending more sustained authority. (5) Voltage operating point — all baselines at V=200 but firmware default is 80, where absolute ceilings are 2.5x lower (step2 at 0.1% error: 0.046 N*m) and the load window that avoids runaway is much narrower; validate at both. (6) Plant simplifications — no back-EMF (fine at standstill only), lumped rigid inertia (no coupling compliance/backlash), heuristic re-stick gate (|tau_drive| < coulomb at |omega|<2e-3): the settled point within the stick band [tau_L-f_s, tau_L+f_s] is trajectory-dependent, so real units will arrest at somewhat different errors than the sim; and real D-term braking on noisy quantized hall counts may be weaker than simulated, deepening the backslip. Bench: calibrated-weight settled-error measurement vs the closed-form/sim predictions (10.2k @ 0.20, 23.3k @ 0.30).
